PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY
Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH) Report

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic fluid
Date Collected: [redacted]
Date Received: [redacted]
Date Reported: [redacted]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal genetic testing requested

TEST PERFORMED
Oligonucleotide Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from cultured amniocytes and analyzed using oligonucleotide array CGH technology. The array platform contains approximately 60,000 genomic probes distributed across the genome. Analysis was performed using the GenSpec 4000 platform with GenomeView software for data interpretation. All genomic coordinates are reported according to the GRCh37/hg19 human genome assembly.

Due to DNA quality limitations, the detection threshold for copy number imbalances was affected, potentially limiting the ability to detect smaller chromosomal imbalances. The array is designed to exclude reporting of imbalances greater than 3Mb in size.

Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) was additionally performed to specifically exclude triploidy.

RESULTS
Array CGH Result: arr(1-22)x2,(XY)x1

No copy number abnormalities detected

The array CGH analysis shows a normal male chromosome complement with no detectable gains or losses of chromosomal material within the resolution limits of this test.

QF-PCR Result: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all markers tested, excluding triploidy.

INTERPRETATION
The array CGH results are consistent with a normal male karyotype. No pathogenic copy number variants were identified within the resolution capabilities of this analysis. The QF-PCR results confirm the absence of triploidy.

LIMITATIONS
- This test cannot detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Low-level mosaicism (<20-30%) may not be detected
- Due to DNA quality constraints, smaller copy number variants may have escaped detection
- The array platform excludes reporting of benign copy number variants >3Mb
- This test does not detect single gene mutations or methylation abnormalities
- Uniparental disomy cannot be detected by this method

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on these results, no further chromosome analysis is recommended on this sample. These findings should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical findings and other diagnostic test results.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by this laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
